conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve had this belly pain for two days now. It’s not like my usual pancreatitis flare, but it’s bad. I’ve been nauseous and threw up a few times, but no blood.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any fevers, chills, or recent travel?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no fever or anything like that. I did have a bowel movement yesterday, but it wasn’t normal—more like small pieces. Haven’t had a real one in weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you’ve been using hydromorphone at home for the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, my PCP prescribed it. I only take it when it’s really bad. I’m not dependent or anything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. We’ll make sure to manage your pain safely. We’ve reviewed your CT from the other hospital—it showed possible partial blockage or severe constipation. We’ll do a quick exam and some tests to clarify.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not my pancreas again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs show no sign of a pancreatitis flare—your amylase and lipase aren’t elevated. That makes it less likely. We’re more concerned about constipation or a partial obstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t been eating much because of the pain. Maybe that’s why I’m backed up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could definitely contribute. We’re going to place a nasogastric tube just in case there’s a blockage, to help relieve any pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds awful. Do I really need it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll try it briefly. If it’s not pulling out much fluid, and you’re passing gas, we can remove it. It’s just a precaution.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve placed the NG tube. It’s not draining much, which is actually a good sign—suggests it’s not a full obstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to give you an enema to help clear out the bowels. If that works and your pain improves, it’ll support that this is constipation-related.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you had a significant bowel movement after the enema. Your abdomen is softer now, and that’s a strong sign we’re on the right track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I feel a bit better already. The pain’s not gone, but it’s way less.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’ll remove the NG tube since it wasn’t draining much and you’re improving. We’ll keep you on IV fluids for now and start you on clear liquids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I eat real food soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start with clear liquids and see how you tolerate them. If no nausea, we’ll advance your diet tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Your labs from last night show your blood sugar is a bit high, but stable. We held your metformin while you were NPO, but we’ll restart it today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had diabetes for years. I check it at home. It’s usually okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep monitoring it. Your blood pressure was a little high on admission, but it’s improved. You’re still on lisinopril, which helps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had high blood pressure for a while. As long as it doesn’t spike, I’m okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The surgery team came by earlier. They agree this looks like severe constipation, not an obstruction. Your KUB showed no blockage, which supports that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I’m not going to need surgery or anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, not at all. You’re improving with conservative treatment—fluids, bowel regimen, and pain control. That’s exactly what we want to see.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been tolerating a soft diet well, no nausea. We’re going to switch you to regular food for dinner if you’re up for it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please. I’m tired of broth and applesauce.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Understood. We’ll also adjust your gabapentin. You were taking it three times a day, but we’re increasing it to every eight hours for better nerve pain control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. It helps with my back pain and the neuropathy from diabetes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a chest X-ray to confirm NG tube placement earlier, but it wasn’t in—probably got dislodged. But since we removed it and you’re doing well, no need to repeat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. I didn’t even feel it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re doing well—you’re ambulatory, eating regular food, and your pain is much better. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What should I do at home to keep this from happening again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re adding Miralax daily and continuing Colace. These will help prevent constipation. Also, stay hydrated and keep moving as tolerated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had gastroparesis in the past. Could that be part of the problem?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly, but right now, the evidence points more to constipation. We’ll let your PCP evaluate if further GI workup is needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your discharge meds will include all your usual ones—ziprasidone, prazosin, omeprazole, and the new stool softeners. Make sure to follow up with your primary doctor soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for helping me feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll get the discharge papers ready. You should be home within a few hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before you leave—your vitals are stable, you’re alert, and you’ve eaten breakfast without issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel ready to go home. I’ll take the Miralax and Colace like you said.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Call your doctor if the pain comes back or you can’t keep food down. Otherwise, you’re good to go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you only if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Appreciate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will bring your prescriptions and discharge instructions shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll read them carefully.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your pain is much improved, but if you need hydromorphone at home, use it sparingly and only as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand. I don’t want to rely on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Focus on the bowel regimen and staying active. That’ll help more in the long run.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I’ll sign the discharge order. You’re all set.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, doc. Really appreciate the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Stay well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.
